thread_text:
sam: Heads up — running long-context soak on mainline and we're seeing steady GPU memory growth tied to the KV page table. Repro on H100, doesn't show on A100. Posting notes and logs here to sync.

lina: Can you paste the exact repro command + model/config? also what runtime revision?

sam: repro: `tools/run_soak --model rw-13b --context 32k --duration 8h --batching=adaptive`
runtime: main @ abc1234 (recent KV paging change). H100 (driver 535.xx) shows ~2GB/hr growth on the host-visible allocator, model kept same tokens, no request rate change. A100 lab runs flat.

ci-bot: test run: https://ci/internal/runs/3201 (soak logs + flamegraphs) :white_check_mark:

raj: Interesting. Could be a classic pagetable/evict ABA — we evict pages while async decoders read them, and PT entries might be recycled. Any "page mismatch" logs?

sam: pasted small log snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T09:12:23Z] kv_pagetable.cpp:warn: PT read gid=42 page=0x7f8ab400 owner=41 expected_owner=42
[2026-03-10T09:12:23Z] kv_pagetable.cpp:debug: evict page=0x7f8ab400 -> free_list pushback
[2026-03-10T09:12:24Z] kv_access.cpp:error: stale_kv_fetch gid=42 token=15324 seq_off=3072
```
small repro also shows intermittent `owner` mismatch.

oliver: H100 vs A100 difference rings a bell — H100 streams and async copy ordering can expose races if we don't have host-side fences. Also H100's memory allocator (or driver caching) tends to reuse freed device pointers faster which can make ABA visible. A100's allocator behavior masks it.

lina: Can you run with extra PT instrumentation: entry generation counter + assert on stale reads? If we see generation toggling it proves ABA. Also try disabling immediate reuse (delay free) as a quick check.

sam: ran w/ gen-counter and 30s delay-free; growth vanished in the 2h smoke. With gen-counter enabled we saw entries flip id:
```
PT[0x7f8ab400] -> gen=102 free -> reallocated -> gen=0 same_ptr
// access later sees owner gid 42 but gen 0 -> stale
```
so ABA confirmed.

marie: This matches the perf regression after `abc1234` — that change moved eviction earlier in the pipeline to reduce tail latency, but likely increased concurrent evict/read overlap. If we moved eviction earlier without stronger ordering, ABA can surface.

raj: Mitigations:
- add generation counter per PT entry (cheap) to detect stale views and fail fast (good for correctness),
- use atomic CAS on install/remove with memory_order_acq_rel + explicit cudaStreamSynchronize for the free path (may hurt perf),
- implement delayed free / quarantine (small time window) to avoid pointer reuse race (low perf cost, high memory cost),
- or change allocator to return zeroed/new pointers on reuse (higher allocator complexity).

oliver: Also check batching heuristics: we changed reuse ordering for KV lookup to favor recently used pages which increases reuse pressure on the same few allocations -> increases pointer reuse frequency. That plus earlier eviction is a bad combo.

lina: For immediate next steps: 1) add gen-counter + assert so we can triage in CI, 2) run bisect between abc1234 and previous to confirm correlation, 3) try quarantine delay in H100 soak for 8h to check stability. If quarantine fixes it, it's a practical short-term mitigation.

sam: I'll run the quarantine soak on H100 tonight and bisect tomorrow morning. Tentative schedule: run q=60s delay-free soak 8h starting 02:00 UTC. I'll upload traces.

oliver: Add a unit test that simulates concurrent evict+read with fake allocator to prevent regressions. Also add a perf flag to measure impact of gen-counter and quarantine in microbench.

marie: Note: if we land quarantine or gen-counter in prod, we need to update billing/cost docs since quarantine increases memory headroom. Also open a bug with P1 if repro in prod.

raj: Long-term: we should prefer a page-table design with an embedded epoch or tagged pointer to avoid ABA entirely and use a reclamation scheme (epoch-based GC) for PT entries. That will scale better than naive delays.

lina: Agreed. For now prioritize correctness + low-effort mitigation. If the bisect proves abc1234 is the trigger, revert or patch that change quickly.

sam: thanks all — I'll post soak results + bisect link here when done. Assigning myself to file the bug with logs if quarantine confirms. :thumbsup:

oliver: thx. If you need GPU time ping infra.

sam: will do.
